title: Annotatio IV §.XI: Bede — left church CORPORALITER; goes as man, remains as God
pass_a_gloss: But he also seriously detested the falsehood, i.e. the corporal presence of Christ, or of His body, both on these earths and in the Sacred Supper: Christ, he says, ascending Victor to the Father after the resurrection, left the Church CORPORALLY, which yet He never stripped of the guard of divine presence (Commentary on Mark Book 4 ch. 13). And on John ch. 14: Those from whom the Lord was departing as man, the same Christ Himself man and God was not leaving. Therefore He was going by that which He was as man, and remaining by that which He was as God. He was going by that which was in one place, and remaining by that which was everywhere.
pass_b_english: Bede also seriously detests the falsehood of a corporal presence of Christ or His body — on earth or in the Sacred Supper.

Ascending Victor after the resurrection He left the Church CORPORALLY, yet never without divine presence. As man He went; as God He remained — going as in one place, remaining as everywhere (Mark 4.13; John 14).
source_text: Sed & falsitatem, i. e. corporalem Christi, sive corporis ejus, tàm in terris hisce, quàm in Cœna S., præsentiam, seriò detestatus: Christus, inquit, ad patrem, post resurrectionem, Victor adscendens, Ecclesiam CORPORALITER reliquit, quam tamen nunquam divinæ præsidio præsentiæ destituit. Comment. in Marcum Lib. 4. cap. 13. Et in Joh. cap. 14. A quibus, ait, homo abscedebat Dominus, eos non relinquebat idem ipse Christus homo & Deus. Ergo ibat per id, quod homo erat, & manebat per id, quod Deus erat. Ibat per id, quod uno loco erat, & manebat per id, quod ubique erat.
